newsitem.title: UK: BA to create jobs at Gatwick, boost services.
newsitem.headline: BA to create jobs at Gatwick, boost services.

text.p: British Airways Plc said on Friday it would create more than 700 permanent new jobs this year at London's Gatwick airport.
Under the airline's recently-announced restructuring plans, around 5,000 British BA workers are expected to take voluntary severance or early retirement this year, BA said in a statement.
BA said it expected to employ around the same number of people by the year 2000 as at present but "with different skills".
BA said 17 new destinations would be added to the Gatwick network by BA and its partners in the next two weeks.
BA said it was transferring its Latin American services -- to Argentina, Brazil, Colombia, Chile, Mexico and Venezuela -- to Gatwick from London Heathrow.
"We are determined to continue to develop the airport as a complementary hub for Heathrow, where we have run out of room to grow," BA chief executive Bob Ayling said.
